claims.heading: orderId namespace and placement context
claims.quotation: The Order ID is a client-managed identifier used to track, modify, and cancel orders. As a result, it must be strictly increasing.
claims.limitation: Execution.orderId says it may not be unique to an account. openOrder describes orderId as the order unique id. orderStatus describes the orderId parameter as the order client id. Those passages are not reconciled here.

claims.heading: orderId reuse across clients and sessions
claims.section_anchor: Open Orders; Master Client ID; Modifying Orders
claims.quotation: the same order can have different API order IDs for different users.
claims.limitation: The sentence is about binding across TWS users. It was not observed in a broker session. It is not a uniqueness result.

claims.heading: orderId across reconnect and restart
claims.section_anchor: Establishing an API connection; Broken API socket connection; Download TWS or IB Gateway
claims.quotation: callback is commonly used to indicate that the connection is completed
claims.limitation: A new connection is documented to receive a next valid order id. Survival of a previous orderId across reconnect or process restart is not stated.

claims.heading: permId absent, null, and zero stay distinct
claims.quotation: The PermId can be 0 for trades originating outside IB.
claims.limitation: Zero is a documented value. Absent and null are not distinguished in the retrieved pages.

claims.heading: permId assignment timing
claims.quotation: The Host order identifier.
claims.limitation: orderBound maps an API order id to what the page calls IBKR permId. When that identifier is assigned is not stated.

claims.heading: permId stability, limits, and standalone non-uniqueness
claims.quotation: The permID returned in the API Order class which is assigned by TWS can be used to identify an order in an account uniquely.
claims.limitation: The sentence is scoped to an account by its own words. Zero is also documented. This is not a global uniqueness guarantee.

claims.heading: execId namespace and duplicates
claims.quotation: Each partial fill has a separate ExecId.
claims.limitation: Identical duplicate payloads for one ExecId are not discussed. Combo orders are documented as a 5-segment sequence.

claims.heading: correction and bust references
claims.quotation: A correction is indicated by an ExecId which differs from a previous ExecId in only the digits after the final period
claims.limitation: The word bust does not appear in the retrieved pages. That absence is not proof that busts are undocumented elsewhere. No reversal or risk release is authorized.

claims.heading: out-of-order execution delivery
claims.limitation: execDetailsEnd marks the end of one response. Delivery order inside that response is not stated.

claims.heading: order status, execution observations, and local attempts
claims.quotation: Often there are duplicate `orderStatus` messages.
claims.limitation: orderStatus and execDetails are separate callbacks in the retrieved text. A local send attempt is not one of those callbacks.

claims.heading: request and response scope
claims.quotation: Requests all current open orders in associated accounts at the current moment.
claims.limitation: TWS execution text also says since midnight, the last 24 hours, and a 7-day Trade Log setting. Those scopes disagree. Web API trades text says the current day and six previous days.

claims.heading: pagination and end of response
claims.quotation: Indicates the end of the Execution reception.
claims.limitation: An end callback is documented. A pagination cursor is not. Live Orders says the endpoint can contain a maximum of 1000 orders. The end of a response is not broker completeness.

claims.heading: retention, truncation, delay, and gaps
claims.quotation: The IB Gateway is limited to only executions from the current trading day since midnight.
claims.limitation: TWS text also mentions a Trade Log setting for the last 7 days. Delay of a single execution is not given a duration.

claims.heading: empty response
claims.quotation: Submission will appear as a blank array.
claims.limitation: The blank array is the documented result of force=true clearing saved information. A 503 is documented when a cancelled or filled order has no cached status. Neither is broker absence.

claims.heading: no completeness token
claims.limitation: Retrieved pages do not present a completeness token. That silence is not proof that no such token exists on an unretrieved page. No completeness token is stored by this task.

claims.heading: reconnect is a new session context
claims.section_anchor: Establishing an API connection; Broken API socket connection
claims.quotation: This function can be used to build reconnection logic or affirm a system disconnect.
claims.limitation: The page does not say that a reconnect creates a new session context. It does say a completed connection supplies account numbers, the next valid order id, and the time of connection.

claims.heading: gateway or TWS restart
claims.section_anchor: What is the IB Gateway?; Execution Details
claims.quotation: Both TWS and IBGW were designed to be restarted daily.
claims.limitation: The same page says that for the TWS API purposes, TWS and IB Gateway are synonymous. The execution page limits IB Gateway to the current trading day since midnight while describing a TWS Trade Log setting. The products are not collapsed here. Version 974+ is a cited autorestart threshold, not a pinned tuple.

claims.heading: disconnect, missing executions, partial fills, and late fills
claims.section_anchor: ExecID Behavior; Broken API socket connection
claims.quotation: Each partial fill has a separate ExecId.
claims.limitation: A partial fill is documented. Which executions are missing after a disconnect, and whether a fill can arrive late, are not stated.

claims.heading: cancel races and conflicting snapshots
claims.quotation: You may still receive an execution while your cancellation request is pending.
claims.limitation: The sentence covers PendingCancel and PreCancelled. Conflicting snapshots are not given a resolution rule.

claims.heading: unknown send before DISPATCH_STARTED
claims.quotation: Indicates that you have transmitted your order, but have not yet received confirmation that it has been accepted by the order destination.
claims.limitation: PendingSubmit is an official status word. It is not the local DISPATCH_STARTED window. No send was performed.

claims.heading: unknown send after DISPATCH_STARTED
claims.limitation: DISPATCH_STARTED does not appear in the retrieved pages.

claims.heading: lost acknowledgement and crash after send
claims.limitation: No retrieved page describes a lost acknowledgement or a crash after send. ARCH-DEC-57 stays in force. No fault injection was performed.

claims.heading: prior writer, lease expiry, and split brain
claims.quotation: This exception will also occur if an API client attempts to connect with a client ID that is already in use.
claims.limitation: A client-id collision is documented. A lease, a prior writer, and split brain are not.

claims.heading: session isolation is external evidence
claims.section_anchor: ClientId 0 and the Master Client ID
claims.quotation: Connecting without using the Master Client ID will mean only trades on the connected Client ID will be returning from calls to the openOrder or execDetails functions.
claims.limitation: This is a documented visibility rule. It was not executed. It is not fencing evidence.

claims.heading: WriterEpoch, adapter session epoch, acceptance, and isolation
claims.limitation: Those four local labels do not appear as IBKR fields in the retrieved pages. Filling one would not fill another.

claims.heading: version, platform, and revalidation
claims.section_anchor: TWS Online or Offline Version?; Paper Trading
claims.quotation: Please use same TWS version to make sure the TWS version and TWS API version are synced.
claims.limitation: No product, API client, platform, operating system, or account-mode tuple is recorded. Paper Trading Account and Live trading environment are named and not selected. No revalidation was run.

claims.heading: a singleton candidate is not authorization
claims.quotation: The order's unique id
claims.limitation: The page uses the word unique. That word is not an authorization and not a uniqueness proof.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqIds
read_candidates.side_effects: Returns the next valid order id through nextValidId. Other effects are not stated.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqExecutions
read_candidates.side_effects: Requests executions matching a filter. The page limits the default window and disagrees about midnight, 24 hours, and 7 days.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqAllOpenOrders
read_candidates.side_effects: Documented as returning open orders once and not initiating a subscription. Not called.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqOpenOrders
read_candidates.side_effects: For client ID 0 this binds manual TWS orders and can change the order ID. The page says it is rejected when API Read-Only Mode is enabled. Not a read.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqAutoOpenOrders
read_candidates.side_effects: autoBind true assigns API order IDs to future manual orders. Not a read.

read_candidates.name: EClient.cancelOrder
read_candidates.side_effects: Cancels an order. Not a read.

read_candidates.name: EClient.reqGlobalCancel
read_candidates.side_effects: Cancels all open orders. Not a read.

read_candidates.name: EClient.placeOrder
read_candidates.side_effects: The modify page says placeOrder with the same order id modifies an open order. Not a read.

read_candidates.name: GET /iserver/account/order/status/{orderId}
read_candidates.side_effects: Documented GET for one order while it remains active. A 503 is documented when no cached status exists. Requires an authenticated brokerage session, which is not authorized.

read_candidates.name: GET /iserver/account/orders
read_candidates.side_effects: The page says filtering prevents websocket sor updates, and force=true clears saved information and yields a blank array. Not a read-only operation. Maximum 1000 orders is documented.

read_candidates.name: GET /iserver/account/trades
read_candidates.side_effects: Documented as the current day and six previous days for the selected account. Not called.

read_candidates.name: POST or account switch /iserver/account
read_candidates.side_effects: The order-status page says the caller must switch the affiliated account before requesting status. Switching the selected account is not a read.
